card.what: Single lever rope clutch for 6 to 12 mm line (Bean's 'Rope Jammer'): holds a halyard or control line on the cabin top so its winch can be freed; lift the lever to let the line run
card.boats: kit part, not yet placed by a layout: halyard and reef-line clutches on a cabin top (a J/22's halyards often lead to clutches or cam cleats aft of the mast; Catalina 22 and bigger boats); ClutchBank is the multi-line version
card.distance: arm's reach in the cockpit and on the cabin top; the camera passes close when you work the halyards
card.before: kit Clutch from bk_parts.clutch (Oct 2026): a tapered black box on a flat base with a flat aluminium handle and a maker's plate

references.use: the look Bean asked for: three-quarter product shot on white (the 'Rope Jammer' tile): grey side plates with a bright edge, a hood-like lever with a ribbed grip over the mouth, red line guide, red release button, lock window, screw heads, a diagonal groove; outline match by angle (photo_outline.py)
references.url: Bean's hardware reference sheet, project upload Nov 8 2026 (measuring and comparing only)

references.use: in use: a bank of five clutches on a small yacht's cabin top, halyards led aft from the mast foot through them
the mechanism (cam, jaws, lever) of a disassembled halyard stopper; not downloaded this round (the image host refused the cloud's requests)

features.text: Two side plates, tallest at the grip end, the top sloping down to the hinge end
A bright strip edging each plate
Lever along the top, hinged at the low end, its ribbed grip turned down over the mouth
Open mouth at the tail end showing the toothed cam
Red flared line guide in the mouth
Red release button in a recess on each plate
Lock window with two tick marks
Four socket screw heads on each plate
Moulded diagonal groove on each plate
Line runs straight through low down, in at the hinge end and out under the grip
Maker's plate on the lever (made-up TERNWAY)
